Gain-of-function mutations in PTPN11 in Noonan syndrome lead to hyperactivation of the RAS/MAPK pathway, resulting in intellectual disability and facial dysmorphism. Similarly, genetic factors on the Y chromosome in 48.XYY syndrome are hypothesized to dysregulate the same RAS/MAPK pathway, potentially leading to overlapping phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in PTPN11 or other RAS/MAPK pathway genes in individuals with 48.XYY syndrome who exhibit these specific phenotypes, or if mutations in PTPN11 are found to have a loss-of-function effect in 48.XYY syndrome. _(variant: Exome or genome sequencing data showing a lack of pathogenic variants in PTPN11 in a cohort of 48.XYY syndrome patients.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared RAS/MAPK pathway dysregulation could lead to common therapeutic strategies targeting pathway hyperactivation for both Noonan syndrome and potentially for some aspects of 48.XYY syndrome, such as developmental delays.
